chapter: Childhood and family in New Orleans
title: Sam's and Isaiah's bands: banjo players and the two Morgan bands
summary: Morgan and Allen try to recall the banjo player and bassists in Sam's band. He explains there were two Morgan bands, including Isaiah's with Jim Little.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Oh, I think so. Yes. He's going that over with the drum. Oh, he was a wonderful drummer, that guy. Oh, my brother had some fine men with him. And during that time, let me see, who played guitar? I'm trying to think who played... It wasn't guitar then. It was banjo. Yeah. It was Johnny. Johnny Dave. Johnny Dave.
I don't know. Was there a fellow by the name of Kimball played? There was an old man, Kimball.
Oh, yeah. I know old man, Kimball, and his son. But he wasn't playing with my brother then. It was... It was a...
It was a fellow by the name of...
Dave. Johnny Dave. I don't know.
It's something like that. Older Brothers or Lower Energy.
Yeah. And let me see now. And before... Now, the bass player was working with him during those big days of my brother. Do you know Sidney Brown? They call him Jim Little.

Jim Little. Yeah. Well, Jim Little was in Isaiah's band. See? That's right. There were two bands. Yeah. See? It was two Morgan bands. That's what I'm trying to break down now. And I... I don't have all that space.
I'm not sure Isaiah can straighten us out. Yeah. He'll give us a good account of that.
